The rage of a new generation inheriting a broken world

WORDS / SUB CULTURE MUSIC

The South African music scene is one that consists of artists from different walks of life, each commenting on what they can musically offer to a society that has endured much change of late.

Floodlights have arrived to throw their hat into the ring of Johannesburg’s alternative music scene. Their music is rooted in punk and grunge, drawing from decades of alternative music with a Floodlights infusion.

The lore of Floodlights begins with a two-person project between guitarist and vocalist Michael and guitarist and violinist Wolf, who were then joined by drummer Sam and Sage, the outfit’s bassist. As a stable line-up, the collective has been curating a sound that moves between raw energy, melodic riffs and experimentation, drawing inspiration from the 70s all the way to the noughties, without merely repeating the sound of yesterday.

For Floodlights, music is about distorted guitars and loud performances, regardless of the audience. These rockers are expressionists of frustration, struggle and the uncertainty that stands before young people today.

Enter the world of Floodlights here

‘We want people to feel the rage of youth set to inherit a broken world,’

Michael bluntly puts it.

His statement is the ideal motif for a musical offering that is restless, unapologetic and consumed with being purposeful. Their sound draws on the attitude of punk, the weight of grunge and the age-old message of being sage to a youth at odds with its cruel reality.

Check out Floodlights’ official YouTube account.

Floodlights are looking to host their own gigs around the Johannesburg area, starting from mid-to-late November until early December 2026, with the potential of collaborating with some of the many talented bands on the local scene. It is an opportunity for them to perform, connect with artists and fans, and lend their service to the Johannesburg alternative music community.

Fans can expect the release of an EP, completed with a mix of already available material and new work that the band will develop from their upcoming gigs. It is another step for the band to confirm their identity, taking their music beyond local stages, with ambitions of reaching international audiences in the near future.

Floodlights are still in development, but they already show great ambition. They understand the flooded scene that they want to break into and are making the necessary moves. With new music and live shows on the horizon, their moment is something we are all anticipating.
